newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed says premier should rule while Yeltsin ill.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says premier should rule while Yeltsin ill.

text.p: Russian national security chief Alexander Lebed said on Friday President Boris Yeltsin should name Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to run the country while the Kremlin leader is unable to fulfil his duties.

"A situation has arisen where someone (Yeltsin) is temporarily unable to carry out his duties. For that period, by his order or decree, a person who would run the country and be responsible for what is going on should be clearly defined and named -- and his name is Chernomyrdin," Lebed told NTV commercial television.
Under the constitution, if the president is incapable of carrying out his duties, the premier stands in for him for up to three months.

But Lebed, who told NTV he had discussed the issue on Friday in talks with Yeltsin's chief of staff Anatoly Chubais, seemed to be saying he wanted Yeltsin to officially name Chernomyrdin, to prevent people acting in the president's name.
"There must be a juridically defined period of time when the president is dealing with his personal affairs and somebody is taking on all obligations to run the country," Lebed said.
A prolonged absence by Yeltsin, who said on Thursday he was to undergo heart surgery, has raised speculation about a struggle for power between Lebed, Chernomyrdin and Chubais.
